en: the amount of money required to maintain ordinary life in a particular place and period
the general level of spending required for housing, food, transport, utilities, healthcare, and other necessities
the expense of maintaining a specified standard or pattern of living
the relative price level of essential goods and services compared across places or periods
changes in household expenses used as a basis for adjusting wages, pensions, or benefits

nuance.ja: cost of living は、単に一世帯が実際に支払った金額ではなく、特定の場所・時期に一定の生活水準を維持するために必要となる一般的な費用水準を表す。living expenses は個人や家庭の具体的な支出項目に焦点を置きやすいのに対し、cost of living は東京と地方、現在と前年などを比較する経済的な尺度としても使われる。standard of living は、所得・住宅・医療・教育・余暇などを含む生活の物質的水準であり、その生活を維持する費用とは異なる。inflation は物価全般の継続的な上昇を表し、cost of living の上昇を引き起こし得るが、両者は完全な同義語ではない。a cost-of-living adjustment は、生活費の変化に応じて賃金・年金・給付などを調整することで、しばしば COLA と略される。
nuance.en: Cost of living does not merely mean the amount one household happened to spend. It describes the general expense required to maintain a given way or standard of life in a particular place and period. Living expenses more readily refers to the specific bills and expenditures of an individual or household, whereas cost of living also functions as an economic basis for comparing cities, countries, or time periods. Standard of living describes the material quality or level of life, including income, housing, healthcare, education, and leisure, rather than the expense required to sustain it. Inflation is a continuing general increase in prices and may raise the cost of living, but the terms are not identical. A cost-of-living adjustment changes wages, pensions, or benefits in response to changing living costs and is often abbreviated to COLA.

purchasing power is the quantity of goods and services that a given amount of money can buy.
a cost-of-living adjustment changes wages, pensions, or benefits in response to changes in living costs.

etymology.ja: cost は古フランス語 cost、現代フランス語 coût に関係し、ラテン語 constare「一定の価格である、成り立つ」にさかのぼる。constare は con-「ともに」と stare「立つ」から成り、価格が確定しているという意味を発達させた。living は古英語 libban「生きる」に由来する live の動名詞・名詞形である。cost of living は文字どおりには「生活することの費用」であり、近代的な物価・賃金・家計の統計が発達するにつれて、一定の生活水準を維持するために必要な費用を表す経済用語として定着した。
etymology.en: Cost came through Old French cost and is related to modern French coût, ultimately deriving from Latin constare, to stand at a fixed price or consist. Constare combines con-, together, with stare, to stand, and developed the idea of an established price. Living is derived from live, from Old English libban, to be alive. Cost of living therefore literally means the expense of living. As modern statistics concerning prices, wages, and household budgets developed, the phrase became established as an economic term for the amount required to maintain a particular standard of life.

note.ja: 個人・家庭が日常生活のために実際に支払う家賃・食費・交通費など。
note.en: The actual housing, food, transport, and other everyday expenses paid by a person or household.

note.en: A close expression referring to the individual costs required to maintain everyday life.

note.en: The housing, food, utility, insurance, and other expenses borne by an entire household.

note.ja: 生活維持のための支出を表す、統計・行政などで使われる比較的形式的な表現。
note.en: A relatively formal term for expenditure required to maintain life, used in statistical or administrative contexts.

note.ja: 消費者が商品・サービスを購入する際に負担する費用を広く表す。
note.en: A broad expression for the costs consumers bear when purchasing goods and services.

grammar.countability: uncountable; normally singular despite ending in -s

usage.singular_agreement: Economics normally takes a singular verb when referring to the academic discipline: Economics is a social science.
usage.no_article: The subject normally appears without an article: study economics, not study the economics.
usage.of_pattern: The economics of something means its costs, revenues, incentives, and overall economic practicality.
usage.discipline: Economics studies how individuals, businesses, governments, and societies allocate scarce resources.
usage.microeconomics: Microeconomics examines choices and interactions involving individuals, households, firms, and particular markets.
usage.macroeconomics: Macroeconomics examines economy-wide matters such as growth, inflation, unemployment, and monetary or fiscal policy.
usage.economy_warning: Economy is the system or condition being studied; economics is the field that studies it.
usage.economic_economical: Economic means relating to the economy; economical usually means efficient or inexpensive.

ja: 限られた資源を人・企業・政府・社会がどのように配分するかを研究する経済学

en: the social science studying how individuals, businesses, governments, and societies allocate scarce resources
the study of the production, distribution, exchange, and consumption of goods and services
the discipline analyzing markets, prices, employment, income, business cycles, and public policy
the costs, revenues, incentives, and commercial viability of a particular project, product, or industry
the study of how choices, incentives, and institutions affect economic outcomes

nuance.ja: economics は語末に -s があるが、学問名としては通常、単数扱いとなり Economics is ... とする。economy が現実の生産・消費・雇用・取引から成る「経済」そのものを表すのに対し、economics はその仕組みを研究する「経済学」である。microeconomics は個人・家庭・企業・特定市場の選択や価格形成を、macroeconomics は経済全体の成長・物価・失業・金融政策・財政政策などを扱う。the economics of a project と言う場合は学問一般ではなく、その事業の費用構造・予想収益・誘因・採算性を意味する。この用法では、技術的に実現可能でも the economics do not work のように、費用に見合わず事業として成立しないことを表せる。ただし、学問名としての基本的な一致は単数である。
nuance.en: Although economics ends in -s, it normally takes singular agreement as the name of an academic discipline: Economics is a social science. Economy denotes the actual system of production, consumption, employment, and exchange, whereas economics is the field that studies how that system operates. Microeconomics examines the choices and interactions of individuals, households, firms, and particular markets. Macroeconomics examines economy-wide matters such as growth, inflation, unemployment, monetary policy, and fiscal policy. In the economics of a project, the word refers not to the discipline generally but to the project’s cost structure, expected revenue, incentives, and commercial viability. In this specialized use, the economics do not work can mean that something is technically possible but not financially sustainable. The discipline itself nevertheless normally takes a singular verb.

economy：国・地域における生産・消費・取引の仕組み、または資源の効率的利用。

an economy is a system of production and consumption or the efficient use of resources.
economic means relating to the economy, economic activity, or commercial viability.
economical means efficient and not requiring unnecessary money, fuel, time, or materials.

macroeconomics studies economy-wide activity, growth, inflation, unemployment, and policy.
finance is the activity or field of raising, managing, lending, and investing money.

etymology.ja: economics は economy に学問分野を表す -ics が付いて成立した。economy はギリシャ語 oikonomia「家政、家の管理」に由来し、oikos「家、世帯」と、nomos「規則、管理」または nemein「配分する、管理する」に関係する要素から成る。もとは世帯の財産・食料・労働などを管理することを意味したが、後に国家・社会全体の生産・交換・資源配分へ対象が広がった。economics は、そのような経済活動の法則と仕組みを体系的に研究する学問の名称となった。
etymology.en: Economics was formed from economy with -ics, a suffix used in the names of fields of study. Economy derives from Greek oikonomia, household management, combining oikos, house or household, with an element related to nomos, rule or management, and nemein, to distribute or administer. The original concept concerned managing a household’s property, food, and labor. Its scope later expanded to the production, exchange, and allocation of resources throughout a state or society. Economics consequently became the name of the systematic discipline studying the mechanisms and principles of such activity.

note.ja: 経済現象を体系的・科学的に研究する分野であることを明示する形式的な表現。
note.en: A formal expression emphasizing the systematic and scientific study of economic phenomena.

note.en: The study of relationships among economics, political institutions, power, and public policy, and a historical name for economics.

usage.definition: An interest rate expresses interest payable or receivable as a proportion of the principal over a specified period.
usage.countable: Interest rate is countable: an interest rate, several interest rates.
usage.on_pattern: Use on to identify the relevant loan, debt, deposit, or account: the interest rate on the mortgage.
usage.percentage: Use of after rate and at before the whole phrase: a rate of five percent; borrowed at an interest rate of five percent.
usage.hyphenation: Hyphenate the phrase when it modifies another noun: an interest-rate increase.
usage.time_basis: The relevant period, such as per year or per month, must be identified when it is not clear from context.
usage.calculation: A quoted interest rate does not by itself show whether interest is simple or compound or whether fees are included.
usage.legal_scope: Disclosure requirements, permitted rates, and calculation methods vary according to jurisdiction, contract, and financial product.

ja: 借入元本に対して一定期間に支払う利息の割合、金利
預金・投資元本に対して受け取る利息の割合
銀行・貸金業者などが融資に適用する利率

元本に対する利息を百分率などで示した数値
en: the proportion of a loan’s principal payable as interest over a specified period
the proportion of a deposit or investment received as interest
the rate charged by a bank or lender for providing credit
a policy or market rate influenced by the monetary-policy decisions of a central bank
a percentage or other ratio expressing interest relative to principal

nuance.ja: interest rate は、元本に対して一定期間に発生する利息の割合である。借り手にとっては借入費用、預金者・投資家にとっては資金を提供することで得る収益率となる。単に five percent と表示されていても、それが年率か月率か、固定か変動か、単利か複利か、手数料を含むかを確認しなければ実際の負担は分からない。fixed interest rate は一定期間変わらない金利、variable または floating interest rate は指標などに応じて変動する金利を表す。nominal interest rate は通常、物価変動を調整していない名目金利で、real interest rate はインフレの影響を考慮した実質金利である。APR は借入費用を比較するための年率表示だが、その法的定義と含まれる費用は制度によって異なり、単純な契約金利と同一とは限らない。
nuance.en: An interest rate is the proportion of principal that accrues as interest over a specified period. For a borrower it represents part of the cost of obtaining credit, while for a depositor or investor it represents a return for supplying funds. A quotation of five percent alone does not reveal the actual cost unless one knows whether the period is annual or monthly, whether the rate is fixed or variable, whether interest is simple or compounded, and whether fees are included. A fixed interest rate remains unchanged for an agreed period, whereas a variable or floating rate changes according to an index or other mechanism. A nominal interest rate normally does not adjust for changes in prices, while a real interest rate takes inflation into account. APR is an annualized measure intended to assist comparison of borrowing costs, but its legal definition and included charges vary and it is not necessarily identical to the contractual interest rate.

ja: interest rate：元本に対して一定期間に支払う、または受け取る利息の割合。

en: an interest rate is the proportion of principal paid or received as interest over a specified period.

a fixed rate ordinarily remains unchanged for a period specified by contract.
a variable rate changes according to a reference rate, index, or contractual mechanism.
an exchange rate is the ratio at which one currency can be exchanged for another.

etymology.ja: interest はラテン語 interesse「間にある、重要である、関係する」に由来し、inter-「間に」と esse「ある」から成る。債権者が返済の遅延などによって被る利害・損失を表す用法から、資金を貸す対価として支払われる金銭の意味が発達した。rate は中世ラテン語 rata「計算された割合」に関係し、ラテン語 reri「計算する、考える」にさかのぼる。interest rate は、利息を元本との比較によって計算した割合を意味する。
etymology.en: Interest derives from Latin interesse, to be between, matter, or concern, combining inter-, between, with esse, to be. A sense involving a creditor’s stake or loss resulting from delayed payment developed into the money paid for the use of borrowed funds. Rate is related to medieval Latin rata, a calculated proportion, ultimately from Latin reri, to calculate or consider. Interest rate therefore denotes the calculated proportion between interest and the principal on which it accrues.

usage.determiner: Before a noun, neither normally modifies a singular countable noun: neither answer, not neither answers.
usage.pronoun: Neither can stand alone for not one and not the other: Neither was suitable.
usage.of_pattern: Neither of is followed by a plural noun phrase or object pronoun: neither of the answers; neither of them.
usage.agreement: Formal usage often prefers a singular verb after neither of, but plural agreement is common when individual members are emphasized, especially in conversation.
usage.correlative: Neither ... nor ... joins two negatively excluded alternatives.
usage.proximity_agreement: With neither ... nor ..., the verb often agrees with the nearer subject, although rewriting may be clearer when the subjects differ in number.
usage.adverbial_agreement: Neither followed by auxiliary–subject inversion expresses agreement with a negative statement: Neither do I.
usage.informal_response: Me neither is a common informal response; Neither do I or Nor do I is more structurally formal.
usage.double_negative: Because neither is already negative, it is normally not combined with another negative verb in standard English.

ja: 二つのうち、どちらも～ない
二人・二個のうち、どちらも該当しないもの
neither A nor B の形で、AもBも～ない
否定文への同意として、自分または別の人にも当てはまらないこと
二つの選択肢・人物・物事をともに否定または除外する語
en: not one and not the other of two people or things
as a pronoun, neither one of two alternatives
in neither A nor B, not A and also not B
as an adverb, likewise not in response to a negative statement
a word used to reject or exclude both of two alternatives

nuance.ja: neither は、原則として二つの選択肢の両方を否定する。neither answer は「二つの答えのどちらも～ない」、neither of the answers は「その二つの答えのどちらも～ない」を意味する。三つ以上をまとめて否定する場合は none of が自然である。ただし、日常英語では二つを厳密に意識せず neither が使われる場合もある。neither ... nor ... は両方を否定する対句で、Neither the buyer nor the seller was ready. のように用いる。二つの主語の数が異なる場合、動詞は近い方の主語に一致させることが多いが、不自然さや曖昧さを避けるため文を書き換えることも望ましい。否定文への同意では Neither do I. のように助動詞と主語を倒置する。Me neither. は非常に自然だが口語的である。
nuance.en: Neither normally excludes both of two alternatives. Neither answer means not either of two answers, while neither of the answers refers explicitly to the two answers as a group. None of is normally preferred when three or more items are being excluded, although everyday usage does not always observe the numerical distinction strictly. Neither ... nor ... creates a paired negative structure, as in Neither the buyer nor the seller was ready. When coordinated subjects differ in number, the verb often agrees with the nearer subject, but rewriting the sentence may avoid awkwardness or ambiguity. In response to a negative statement, neither takes auxiliary–subject inversion: Neither do I. Me neither is extremely natural in conversation but more informal.

ja: neither：二つのうちどちらも～ない、または否定文に「私も～ない」と同意する。
either：二つのうちどちらか一方。または否定文で「どちらも～ない」の範囲を作る。
none：通常、三つ以上または数量を限定しない集合の中で一つも～ない。
both：二つの人・物の双方。
neither ... nor ...：AもBも～ない。
either ... or ...：AかBのどちらか。
Neither do I.：否定文に対する「私もそうではない」という比較的整った応答。
Me neither.：否定文に対する「私も」の口語的な応答。
en: neither means not either of two alternatives or expresses agreement with a negative statement.
either means one or the other of two alternatives and also occurs within the scope of a negative.
none normally means not one of three or more items or of a group whose size is unspecified.
both means the two people or things considered together.
neither ... nor ... excludes both A and B.
either ... or ... presents A and B as alternatives.
Neither do I is a structurally formal way to agree with a negative statement.
Me neither is an informal conversational response meaning that the negative statement also applies to the speaker.

etymology.ja: 古英語 nawþer、næþer などの形に由来し、否定を表す要素と ægþer「二つのうちどちらか、各々」が結び付いた語である。後半は現代英語の either と歴史的に対応する。したがって neither の基本構造は「二つのうち、どちらでもない」である。nor も否定を表す接続的な語として組み合わされ、neither ... nor ... という対応構文が定着した。
etymology.en: Neither derives from Old English forms such as nawther and næther, combining a negative element with ægther, either or each of two. The latter element is historically related to modern either. The basic structure of neither therefore means not either one of two. Nor developed as a coordinating negative partner, producing the established correlative construction neither ... nor ....

note.en: Emphasizes that not even one of the two alternatives applies.

usage.determiner: Before a noun, either normally modifies a singular countable noun: either answer, not either answers.
usage.pronoun: Either can stand alone for either one of two alternatives: Either will be acceptable.
usage.of_pattern: Either of is followed by a plural noun phrase or object pronoun: either of the answers; either of them.
usage.agreement: Formal usage often prefers a singular verb after either of, although plural agreement occurs in informal English.
usage.correlative: Either ... or ... presents two alternatives, possibilities, or coordinated elements.
usage.proximity_agreement: With either ... or ..., a verb often agrees with the nearer subject; rewriting can be clearer when the subjects differ in number.
usage.negative_adverb: At the end of a negative clause, either means also: I don’t know either.
usage.both_sides: Either can mean each of two in expressions such as on either side of the road, which commonly means on both sides.
usage.two_alternatives: Either traditionally concerns two alternatives; any is generally preferred when selecting freely from three or more.

nuance.ja: either は原則として二つの選択肢を扱い、「どちらか一方」または「どちらでも」を表す。You can choose either option. は二つの選択肢のどちらを選んでもよいという意味で、Choose either A or B. はAかBのいずれか一つを選ぶことを明示する。either of the options の後では、形式的な英語では単数動詞が好まれるが、会話では複数動詞も見られる。on either side の either は「片側だけ」ではなく、通常「両側に」を意味する点に注意が必要である。否定文の末尾では also の否定形に相当し、I don’t like it either. は「私もそれが好きではない」となる。either ... or ... で主語を結ぶ場合、動詞は近い方の主語に一致することが多いが、単複が混在すると不自然になりやすいため、文を書き換える方が明確な場合もある。
nuance.en: Either normally concerns two alternatives and means one or the other or whichever of the two is chosen. You can choose either option permits the selection of either one, while Choose either A or B explicitly presents the two alternatives. After either of, formal English generally prefers a singular verb, although plural agreement occurs in conversation. In on either side, either commonly means each of the two and therefore both sides, not merely one side. At the end of a negative clause, either corresponds to also under negation: I don’t like it either. When either ... or ... coordinates subjects, the verb often agrees with the nearer subject, but a sentence containing subjects of different numbers may be clearer if rewritten.

ja: either：二つのうちどちらか一方、どちらでも、または否定文で「～もまた…ない」。
neither：二つのうちどちらも～ない、または否定文への「私も～ない」という同意。
both：二つの人・物を合わせた双方。
any：三つ以上を含む集合から、どれでも・誰でも。
either ... or ...：AかBのどちらか。

also：肯定文で「～もまた」を表す。
too：通常、肯定文の末尾で「～もまた」を表す口語的な語。
en: either means one or the other of two, whichever one is chosen, or also not in a negative clause.
neither means not either of two alternatives or expresses agreement with a negative statement.
both means the two people or things considered together.
any permits selection from a group that may contain three or more alternatives.
either ... or ... presents A and B as alternatives.
neither ... nor ... excludes both A and B.
also adds a person, thing, or fact in an affirmative statement.
too commonly means also at the end of an affirmative clause.

etymology.ja: 古英語 ægþer「二つの各々、二つのうちどちらか」に由来する。この語は「常に、いずれも」に関係する要素と、「二つのうちどちら」を表す要素から形成されたとされる。もともと「二つの各々」という意味と「二つのうちどちらか」という意味の双方を持っていたため、現代英語でも either option「どちらかの選択肢」と on either side「両側に」という二つの用法が共存している。否定形 neither も歴史的に同じ語を基礎としている。
etymology.en: Either derives from Old English ægther, meaning each of two or one of two. The formation contained elements associated with each or always and with which of two. Because the earlier word could mean both each of the two and one or the other of the two, modern English retains both uses: either option means whichever one of two options, while on either side commonly means on each of the two sides. The negative form neither developed historically from the same base.

note.ja: 数を二つに限定せず、集合の中のどれでもよいことを表す。
note.en: Allows selection from a group without limiting the number of alternatives to two.

usage.determiner: Before a noun, whichever means any one or group selected from a limited set: whichever route you choose.
usage.pronoun: Whichever can stand without a following noun: Take whichever you prefer.
usage.fused_relative: It can introduce a clause that functions as a noun phrase: Whichever is cheaper will be acceptable.
usage.of_pattern: Whichever of is followed by a plural noun phrase or object pronoun: whichever of the proposals; whichever of them.
usage.number: Unlike either, whichever is not inherently limited to two alternatives and can refer to any number in a defined set.
usage.agreement: Verb agreement depends on the number of the noun or referent: whichever option is; whichever applicants are selected.
usage.no_matter_which: In concessive use, whichever can mean no matter which: Whichever way you approach it, the result is the same.
usage.limited_choice: Whichever normally implies a known or contextually limited range of alternatives; whatever is broader and less restricted.

en: any one selected from a known or limited group of alternatives
the particular alternative that is eventually chosen or proves applicable
no matter which person, thing, method, or possibility is involved
a word indicating that the result remains the same regardless of the alternative selected
as a pronoun, whichever one or ones the person prefers

nuance.ja: whichever は、文脈上分かっている複数の選択肢から「どれを選んでも」「実際に選ばれるどれか」を表す。Choose whichever seat you like. なら、利用可能な座席の中から好きなものを選べる。either は原則として二つのうちどちらかを指すが、whichever は二つに限定されず、三つ以上の選択肢にも使える。which は話者が選択肢を尋ねる語であるのに対し、whichever は選択を相手に委ねたり、どの選択でも結果が同じであることを示したりする。whatever は対象の範囲が明示されていない場合にも使える、より広い語である。Whichever comes first や whichever is earlier は、契約・規則・日程説明で二つ以上の基準のうち最初に成立するものを指定する便利な表現である。
nuance.en: Whichever refers to any alternative selected from a group understood from context or to the particular alternative that ultimately applies. Choose whichever seat you like permits selection from the available seats. Either is traditionally limited to one of two alternatives, whereas whichever can be used with two, three, or more. Which asks the speaker or listener to identify an alternative, while whichever leaves the choice open or indicates that the result does not depend on the selection. Whatever is broader and can refer to a thing or course of action without a clearly defined set of alternatives. Whichever comes first and whichever is earlier are particularly useful in contracts, rules, and schedules for identifying the first of two or more possible events or dates.

ja: whichever：既知・限定された選択肢の中からどれを選んでも、または実際に該当するどれか。

either means one or the other of two alternatives or whichever of the two is chosen.
whatever means anything or no matter what, without requiring a clearly limited set.

etymology.ja: which に、選択の自由または「～であっても」を表す ever が付いて成立した。which は古英語 hwilc「どの、どのような」に由来し、歴史的には who と like に対応する要素を含む。ever は古英語 æfre「常に、いつでも」に由来する。この組合せにより、whichever は「いずれのものを選ぶ場合であっても」「実際にどのものが該当しようとも」という意味を持つようになった。whoever、whatever、wherever、whenever も同様の形成を持つ。
etymology.en: Whichever was formed from which and ever. Which derives from Old English hwilc, which or what kind of, and historically contains elements related to who and like. Ever comes from Old English æfre, always or at any time. Their combination produced the sense no matter which one is selected or whichever one ultimately proves relevant. Whoever, whatever, wherever, and whenever follow the same general pattern of formation.

grammar.transitivity: not applicable as a noun; reflate can be transitive or intransitive

usage.policy_sense: Reflation can mean deliberate monetary or fiscal stimulation intended to raise demand, output, employment, and the price level after weakness or deflation.
usage.outcome_sense: It can also describe the resulting recovery of prices, inflation expectations, nominal spending, or economic activity.
usage.uncountable: The word is normally uncountable: pursue reflation; signs of reflation.
usage.technical_scope: Technical usage may specifically refer to restoring a depressed price level toward its previous trend.
usage.inflation_contrast: Reflation is generally a recovery from deficient demand or abnormally low prices and does not necessarily mean uncontrolled or excessive inflation.
usage.policy_tools: Depending on context, reflationary measures may include lower interest rates, increased money or credit availability, tax reductions, or higher government spending.
usage.market_use: A reflation trade is an investment strategy based on expectations of strengthening growth, prices, and nominal activity.
usage.register: Reflation is specialized economic and financial vocabulary and is uncommon in ordinary conversation.

ja: 景気低迷・デフレの後、需要・生産・雇用・物価水準を回復させる政策
金融緩和・財政刺激などによって経済活動を再び拡大させること
低下した物価水準を従来の傾向または望ましい水準へ戻すこと
デフレまたは低インフレから、物価・賃金・名目成長が回復する局面
景気と物価の回復を予想して資産価格などが動く市場環境
en: policy intended to restore demand, output, employment, and prices after economic weakness or deflation
the stimulation of economic activity through expansionary monetary or fiscal measures
the restoration of a depressed price level toward its previous trend or a desired level
a phase in which prices, wages, inflation expectations, and nominal growth recover from unusually low levels
a market environment shaped by expectations of stronger growth and rising prices

nuance.ja: reflation は、単に物価が上昇する inflation と異なり、景気低迷・需要不足・デフレなどによって低下した経済活動や物価水準を、政策によって回復させるという意味を持つ。金融政策では金利引下げや資金供給の拡大、財政政策では政府支出の増加や減税などが reflationary measures となり得る。狭い技術的用法では、物価水準が長期的な傾向線を下回った後、その水準へ戻ることを指す。したがって、reflation は通常、デフレからの正常化または景気回復の初期段階として肯定的・中立的に語られ、直ちに制御不能なインフレを意味しない。ただし刺激が過度または長期化すれば、望ましい回復を超えて高インフレへつながる可能性はある。金融市場の reflation trade は、成長・物価・金利の上昇を見込んで、それによって利益を得やすい資産へ投資する戦略を表す。
nuance.en: Unlike inflation, which simply denotes a rise in the general price level, reflation carries the idea of restoring economic activity and prices after recession, deficient demand, or deflation. Lower interest rates and increased liquidity may serve as monetary reflationary measures, while greater government spending or tax reductions may provide fiscal reflation. In a narrower technical sense, reflation is the recovery of a price level that has fallen below its longer-term trend. It is therefore often presented neutrally or positively as normalization following deflation or as an early phase of recovery and does not automatically imply excessive or uncontrolled inflation. If stimulus becomes too strong or persists too long, however, the recovery may develop into undesirably high inflation. In financial markets, a reflation trade is a strategy designed to benefit from expectations of stronger growth, rising prices, and often higher interest rates.

ja: reflation：低迷・デフレ後の需要・経済活動・物価水準を政策によって回復させること。
inflation：商品・サービスの一般的な価格水準が継続的に上昇すること。
deflation：一般的な価格水準が広範かつ持続的に下落すること。
disinflation：物価は上昇しているが、その上昇率が低下すること。
economic recovery：景気後退や低迷の後、経済活動が改善・回復する過程。
monetary easing：金利引下げや資金供給によって金融環境を緩和すること。
fiscal stimulus：政府支出・減税などによって総需要と経済活動を刺激すること。
stimulus：経済活動を活発にするための政策的な刺激策を広く表す。
en: reflation is policy-led restoration of demand, economic activity, and prices after weakness or deflation.
inflation is a continuing increase in the general price level of goods and services.
deflation is a broad and persistent decline in the general price level.
disinflation is a reduction in the rate of inflation while prices generally continue to rise.
economic recovery is the process of improving after recession or prolonged weakness.
monetary easing relaxes financial conditions through lower rates, additional liquidity, or similar measures.
fiscal stimulus uses government spending, tax reductions, or related measures to strengthen aggregate demand.
stimulus is the broad term for policy action intended to increase economic activity.

etymology.ja: reflation は re-「再び、元へ」と inflation から作られた経済用語である。inflation はラテン語 inflare「吹き込む、膨らませる」に由来し、in-「中へ」と flare「吹く」から成る。経済上の inflation が通貨量や物価水準の膨張を表すようになった後、低下した価格・需要・経済活動を再び膨らませ、以前の水準へ戻す政策または過程を表すため reflation が形成された。したがって、語の構造上も単なる継続的な物価上昇より「再び膨らませる」という回復の意味が強い。
etymology.en: Reflation was formed from re-, again or back, and inflation. Inflation derives from Latin inflare, to blow into or expand, combining in-, into, with flare, to blow. After inflation became an economic term for expansion in money or the price level, reflation was created to describe deliberately expanding depressed demand, prices, or activity again and restoring them toward an earlier or desired path. Its structure therefore emphasizes renewed expansion or recovery rather than an indefinite continuation of rising prices.

note.ja: 金融・財政措置によって需要・生産・雇用などを活性化させる政策全般。
note.en: The broad use of monetary or fiscal measures to strengthen demand, output, and employment.

note.ja: 金利引下げ・資金供給などによって借入れや支出を促す金融政策。
note.en: Monetary policy that lowers rates or increases liquidity to encourage borrowing and spending.

note.ja: 政府支出の増加・減税などによって総需要を拡大する財政政策。
note.en: Fiscal policy that expands aggregate demand through increased public spending, tax reductions, or similar measures.

note.ja: 景気後退・不況・低迷の後に、生産・雇用・所得などが改善する過程。
note.en: The process in which production, employment, and income improve after recession or weakness.

note.ja: 下落または低迷していた一般物価水準が以前の傾向・水準へ戻ること。
note.en: The return of a depressed general price level toward its former level or trend.

ja: The government adopted a policy of reflation to revive demand after years of deflation. — 政府は長年のデフレ後に需要を回復させるため、リフレーション政策を採用した。
Lower interest rates and increased public spending contributed to the reflation of the economy. — 金利引下げと政府支出の増加が、経済の回復と物価の押上げに寄与した。
Reflation does not necessarily mean that inflation has become excessive. — リフレーションは、インフレが過度になったことを必ずしも意味しない。
Investors began a reflation trade as expectations of stronger growth and higher prices increased. — 成長加速と物価上昇への期待が強まると、投資家はリフレーション取引を始めた。
Reflation may encourage companies to resume investment in research, patents, and new trademarks after a prolonged downturn. — リフレーションによって、企業が長期的な景気低迷後に研究・特許・新規商標への投資を再開する可能性がある。
en: The government adopted a policy of reflation to revive demand after years of deflation.
Lower interest rates and increased public spending contributed to the reflation of the economy.
Reflation does not necessarily mean that inflation has become excessive.
Investors began a reflation trade as expectations of stronger growth and higher prices increased.
Reflation may encourage companies to resume investment in research, patents, and new trademarks after a prolonged downturn.

usage.policy: Reflationary describes policy intended to raise demand, output, employment, prices, or inflation expectations after economic weakness or deflation.
usage.conditions: It can also describe economic or market conditions characterized by recovering growth, prices, wages, and nominal activity.
usage.effect: A measure may be called reflationary when it is expected to move depressed activity or prices upward.
usage.inflationary_contrast: Inflationary broadly means causing or associated with rising prices, whereas reflationary usually implies recovery from deficient demand, deflation, or unusually low inflation.
usage.attributive: The word is used mainly before a noun: reflationary policy or a reflationary environment.
usage.predicative: Predicative use is also possible: The proposed tax cut may be reflationary.
usage.comparison: Comparative forms are grammatically possible but relatively uncommon outside economic analysis.
usage.register: The word is specialized and occurs mainly in economics, central-bank communication, financial journalism, and investment analysis.

ja: 景気低迷・デフレ後に、需要・生産・雇用・物価の回復を促す
金融緩和・財政刺激などによって経済を再び拡大させる

en: intended to restore demand, output, employment, and prices after economic weakness or deflation
stimulating renewed economic expansion through monetary or fiscal policy
causing unusually low prices, inflation, or inflation expectations to rise
relating to conditions in which growth, wages, prices, and nominal income recover together
relating to an investment strategy intended to benefit from economic and price recovery

nuance.ja: reflationary は、景気後退・需要不足・デフレなどの後に、経済活動と物価水準を回復させる政策・圧力・環境を表す。reflationary monetary policy なら、金利引下げや資金供給の拡大などによって需要と物価を押し上げる金融政策、reflationary fiscal policy なら、政府支出の増加や減税による刺激策を意味する。inflationary は物価上昇を引き起こすものを広く表し、その物価上昇が望ましいか過度かを問わない。これに対し reflationary は、低迷した経済や低すぎる物価を正常な軌道へ戻すという回復的な含みを持つ。ただし、reflationary policy が予想以上に強く作用すれば、過度な inflationary pressure を生む可能性もある。投資の文脈では、reflationary trade や reflationary strategy が、成長・物価・金利の上昇から利益を得ることを狙う取引を表す。
nuance.en: Reflationary describes a policy, pressure, or environment that restores economic activity and prices after recession, deficient demand, or deflation. Reflationary monetary policy may involve lower interest rates or increased liquidity intended to strengthen demand and prices. Reflationary fiscal policy may involve increased government spending or tax reductions. Inflationary broadly describes anything causing prices to rise, without indicating whether the increase is a desirable recovery or an excessive development. Reflationary, by contrast, carries the restorative implication of returning a depressed economy or an abnormally low price level toward a more normal path. A reflationary policy that proves stronger than expected may nevertheless generate excessive inflationary pressure. In investment language, a reflationary trade or strategy seeks to benefit from rising growth, prices, and often interest rates.

ja: reflationary：景気低迷・デフレ後の需要・経済活動・物価の回復を促す。
inflationary：物価上昇を引き起こす、またはインフレを伴う。

expansionary：経済活動・信用・需要などを拡大させる。
stimulative：経済・活動・反応などを刺激して活発にする。
accommodative：特に金融政策が、低金利などによって経済活動を支援する。
contractionary：需要・信用・経済活動などを抑制・縮小させる。
en: reflationary promotes recovery in demand, economic activity, and prices after weakness or deflation.
inflationary causes or is associated with a rise in the general price level.
deflationary reduces demand, wages, or prices and contributes to deflation.
disinflationary lowers the rate of price increases without necessarily causing prices themselves to fall.
expansionary increases economic activity, credit, demand, or the money supply.
stimulative encourages greater economic activity or another form of response.
accommodative describes policy, especially monetary policy, that supports activity through favorable financial conditions.
contractionary restrains or reduces demand, credit, or economic activity.

etymology.ja: reflation に、性質・関係を表す形容詞接尾辞 -ary が付いて成立した。reflation 自体は re-「再び、元へ」と inflation から作られた。inflation はラテン語 inflare「吹き込む、膨らませる」に由来する。したがって reflationary は、低下した需要・生産・物価などを「再び膨らませる」性質または効果を持つことを語構成上表している。
etymology.en: Reflationary was formed from reflation with the adjective-forming suffix -ary, indicating relation or character. Reflation itself combines re-, again or back, with inflation. Inflation ultimately derives from Latin inflare, to blow into or expand. Reflationary therefore literally characterizes something capable of expanding depressed demand, output, prices, or nominal activity again.

note.ja: 金融・財政政策などが需要・信用・生産を拡大させることを広く表す。
note.en: Broadly describes monetary or fiscal policy that increases demand, credit, production, or economic activity.

note.ja: 需要・投資・雇用などを刺激し、活動を活発にする。
note.en: Encourages stronger demand, investment, employment, or economic activity.

note.ja: 特に金融政策が、低金利や潤沢な資金供給によって経済活動を支える。
note.en: Especially of monetary policy, supports activity through low rates or ample liquidity.

note.ja: 経済成長を促進または支援することを目的とする。
note.en: Intended to promote or support economic growth.

note.ja: 物価を押し上げる性質を表すが、デフレ後の回復という含みは必須ではない。
note.en: Describes a tendency to raise prices without necessarily implying recovery from deflation or weakness.

grammar.transitivity: prepositional transitive; cope alone is intransitive
patterns: cope with the fact that + clause
be able / unable to cope with + noun
find it difficult to cope with + noun

usage.preposition: Use with before the difficulty or situation: cope with pressure.
usage.gerund: After with, use a noun or gerund: cope with working long hours, not cope with work long hours.
usage.inseparability: The expression is not separable: cope with the problem, not cope the problem with.
usage.cope_alone: Cope can be used without an object when the difficulty is understood: I’m not sure I can cope.
usage.success: Cope usually means managing a difficult situation sufficiently, not necessarily solving or eliminating it.
usage.ability: Can cope with often expresses having enough practical or emotional capacity to deal with something.
usage.cope_up_warning: Cope up with occurs in some regional varieties, but cope with is the standard form in international English.
usage.register: Natural in both everyday and professional communication.

ja: 困難・問題・ストレスなどにうまく対処する
厳しい状況に耐えながら、必要な行動や生活を続ける
仕事量・需要・変化などを処理できる能力を持つ
感情的な苦痛や不安を受け止め、何とか乗り切る
問題を完全に解決できなくても、支障を抑えて対応する
en: to deal successfully enough with a difficult problem, situation, or source of stress
to continue functioning despite demanding or unpleasant circumstances
to have sufficient capacity to manage a workload, level of demand, or change
to endure and manage emotional pain, anxiety, or pressure
to limit the adverse effects of a problem even when it cannot be completely solved

nuance.ja: cope with は、困難な状況を完全に解決・克服するというより、その負担に耐えながら何とか機能し続けることを表す。She coped with the pressure. は、圧力そのものを取り除いたのではなく、その状況下でも必要な行動ができたという意味である。deal with は問題への対応全般を表し、解決の成否を問わない場合もある。handle は状況を管理・処理できる能力に焦点を置き、cope with より自信のある響きになりやすい。overcome は困難に打ち勝ち、障害を乗り越えるという、より完全な成功を示す。感情・病気・喪失などについて cope with を使うときは、その人が弱いと断定するのではなく、継続的な適応過程を表せる。否定形 can’t cope は、負担が能力を超えているという強い表現になり得る。
nuance.en: Cope with generally means continuing to function under a difficult burden rather than completely solving or defeating it. She coped with the pressure indicates that she remained able to do what was required, not that the pressure disappeared. Deal with broadly describes responding to a matter and may say nothing about whether the response succeeds. Handle often emphasizes competence and control and can sound more confident than cope with. Overcome indicates a more complete victory over a difficulty or obstacle. When used of grief, illness, or emotional stress, cope with can describe an ongoing process of adaptation without judging the person as weak. The negative can’t cope may strongly suggest that the demands of the situation have exceeded someone’s present capacity.

ja: cope with：困難・ストレスを抱えながら、何とか対処して機能し続ける。
deal with：問題・人物・状況に対応することを広く表し、成功は必ずしも含意しない。
handle：問題・仕事・人物などを適切に管理・処理する能力を強調する。
manage：困難があっても、必要なことを何とか成し遂げる。
overcome：困難・恐怖・障害などに打ち勝ち、乗り越える。
adapt to：新しい環境・条件に合わせて行動や考え方を変える。
put up with：不快な人・状況を、嫌でも我慢する。
get through：困難な期間・経験・仕事などを最後まで乗り切る。
en: cope with means continuing to function while managing difficulty, pressure, or stress.
deal with broadly means responding to a problem, person, or situation without necessarily implying success.
handle emphasizes the ability to manage or control a task, person, or difficult situation.
manage means succeeding in doing what is necessary despite difficulty.
overcome means defeating or moving beyond a difficulty, fear, or obstacle.
adapt to means changing behavior or methods to suit new conditions.
put up with means tolerating an unpleasant person or situation despite disliking it.
get through means surviving or completing a difficult period, experience, or task.

etymology.ja: cope は中期英語 copen「争う、立ち向かう」に由来し、古フランス語 couper「打つ」と関係すると考えられている。初期には敵と戦う、打ち合うという意味を持ち、そこから困難な相手・状況に立ち向かう意味へ発達した。後に with を伴って、問題・圧力・変化などに対処し、何とか切り抜けるという現代的な cope with の用法が定着した。
etymology.en: Cope derives from Middle English copen, to contend or encounter, and is generally connected with Old French couper, to strike. Its earlier meanings involved fighting or meeting an opponent in combat. The word then developed the figurative sense of confronting and managing a difficult situation. With subsequently became established as the preposition introducing the problem, pressure, or change being managed, producing the modern construction cope with.

note.ja: 問題・課題・人物などに対応することを広く表し、結果が成功かどうかは必ずしも示さない。
note.en: Broadly means responding to a problem, task, or person without necessarily indicating a successful outcome.

note.ja: 困難な仕事・状況・人物を能力をもって管理し、適切に処理する。
note.en: To manage a difficult task, situation, or person competently and with control.

note.ja: 困難な条件下でも、必要なことをどうにか実行・達成する。
note.en: To succeed in doing what is necessary despite difficult conditions.

note.ja: 苦痛・困難・不快な状況に耐え、持ちこたえる。
note.en: To continue through pain, difficulty, or an unpleasant situation without giving up.

note.ja: 複雑な状況・制度・問題の中で、慎重に進路を選びながら対処する。
note.en: To find a workable course through a complex situation, system, or problem.

equivalents.it: far fronte a / riuscire a gestire

ja: She found it difficult to cope with the pressure of her new position. — 彼女は新しい役職の重圧に対処することが難しいと感じた。
The hospital hired additional staff to cope with increased demand. — 病院は増加した需要に対応するため、職員を増員した。

The patent department introduced new software to cope with the growing number of filing deadlines. — 特許部門は、増加する出願期限の管理に対応するため、新しいソフトウェアを導入した。

grammar.transitivity: mainly transitive; intransitive when describing how a vehicle, machine, or material responds to control
patterns: be able / unable to handle + noun
get / have a handle on + noun

usage.manage: Handle a problem or task means manage, control, or deal with it competently.
usage.person: Handle a person can mean manage the person’s behavior or communicate with them effectively, but it may sound controlling in some contexts.
usage.touch: Handle an object means touch, hold, move, or work with it using the hands.
usage.commercial: Handle goods, information, payments, or applications means receive, process, manage, or be responsible for them.
usage.intransitive: A vehicle or machine handles well when it responds well to control.
usage.noun_object: As a noun, a handle is the part designed to be held when opening, lifting, or controlling something.
usage.understanding: Get a handle on something means develop sufficient understanding or control of it.
usage.name: A handle can informally mean a name, nickname, call sign, or online username.

ja: 問題・状況・仕事などを適切に処理・管理する
人・顧客・苦情などに対応し、必要なやり取りを行う
物を手で持つ・触る・動かす・取り扱う
商品・情報・支払い・申請などを受け付け、処理する
乗り物・機械などを操作・制御する
名詞として、扉・容器・道具などを持つための取っ手・柄
口語的に、人の名前・あだ名・オンライン上のユーザー名
en: to manage or deal competently with a problem, situation, or task
to deal with a person, customer, complaint, or communication
to touch, hold, move, or work with an object using the hands
to receive, process, manage, or take responsibility for goods, information, payments, or applications
to operate or control a vehicle, machine, or instrument
as a noun, the part of a door, container, or tool designed to be held
informally, a person’s name, nickname, call sign, or online username

nuance.ja: 動詞 handle の中心は、対象を手の内に置き、適切に扱うことである。物理的に物を「手で扱う」という意味から、問題・仕事・人物・情報などを管理・処理する意味へ広がった。I can handle it. は、単に問題へ対応するだけでなく、「自分に任せてよい、対処する能力がある」という自信を表す。cope with は困難な負担に耐えながら何とか機能することを強調するのに対し、handle は状況を制御し、必要な処理を行う能力を感じさせやすい。handle a person は「その人にうまく対処する」を意味するが、人を物のように管理する響きになることもある。名詞の get a handle on は、複雑な問題を理解・制御できる段階へ到達することを表す。SNSなどの handle は、他の利用者がその人を識別するためのユーザー名である。
nuance.en: The core idea of handle is bringing something under one’s hand and dealing with it appropriately. The physical meaning of touching or manipulating an object developed into the figurative sense of managing problems, tasks, people, and information. I can handle it expresses not merely willingness to respond but confidence that the speaker has the capacity to take control of the matter. Cope with emphasizes continuing to function under difficulty or stress, whereas handle more readily suggests competence, control, and effective processing. Handle a person can mean deal effectively with them, but it may sound as though the person is being managed like an object. The noun phrase get a handle on means reach a sufficient level of understanding or control. On social media, a handle is a username by which other users identify an account.

ja: handle：問題・仕事・人物などを能力をもって処理する、または物を手で扱う。
cope with：困難・ストレスを抱えながら、何とか対処して機能し続ける。
deal with：問題・人物・状況に対応することを広く表し、成功は必ずしも含意しない。
manage：人・組織・状況を管理する、または困難でも何とか成し遂げる。
process：情報・申請・支払いなどを所定の手順で処理する。
operate：機械・装置・システムを動かし、その機能を利用する。
touch：身体、特に手を物に接触させる。
grip：手で物をしっかり握る、または握るための部分。
en: handle means managing a problem or person competently or physically touching and manipulating an object.
cope with means continuing to function while managing difficulty, pressure, or stress.
deal with broadly means responding to a problem, person, or situation without necessarily implying success.
manage means controlling a person or organization or succeeding despite difficulty.
process means treating information, applications, or payments according to an established procedure.
operate means controlling a machine, device, or system so that it performs its function.
touch means bringing part of the body, especially a hand, into contact with something.
grip means holding something firmly or the part designed to provide a secure hold.

etymology.ja: 古英語 hand「手」を基礎として中英語期に成立した handel「手で触れる部分、取っ手」に由来する。もともとは道具・容器・扉などを手でつかむための部分を表した。そこから「取っ手を持つ」「手で扱う」という動詞が生まれ、さらに物事を自分の管理下に置くという比喩によって、問題・仕事・人物・情報などを処理する意味へ発達した。人名・ユーザー名を表す口語的な handle も、人や物を識別してつかむ手掛かりという発想に関係する。
etymology.en: Handle was formed from hand and derives from Middle English handel, a part held by the hand. It originally referred to the part of a tool, container, or door designed to be grasped. From this noun developed the verb meaning to hold, touch, or manipulate with the hands. The physical idea was then extended metaphorically to bringing a problem, task, person, or body of information under one’s control. The informal sense of a name or username similarly treats a handle as a means by which a person or thing can be identified and figuratively grasped.

note.ja: 仕事・組織・状況を管理する、または困難なことを何とか成し遂げる。
note.en: To control work, an organization, or a situation, or to succeed in doing something difficult.

note.ja: 問題・課題・人物などに対応することを広く表す。
note.en: A broad expression for responding to a problem, matter, task, or person.

note.ja: 申請・情報・注文・支払いなどを一定の手順に従って処理する。
note.en: To deal with an application, information, order, or payment according to an established procedure.

note.ja: 物・器具を手や機械で巧みに動かす。人に用いると不当に操る意味になり得る。
note.en: To move an object or instrument skillfully; when applied to people, it can mean controlling them unfairly.

note.ja: 機械・状況・過程などの動きや結果を指揮・制限する。
note.en: To direct or limit the operation, movement, or outcome of a machine, situation, or process.

patterns: ask someone to bear with + person
thank someone for bearing with + person
if you’ll bear with me, + clause
you’ll have to bear with me
bear with me for a moment

usage.object: The object is normally the person who needs patience: bear with me or bear with us.
usage.inseparability: The expression is inseparable: bear with me, not bear me with.
usage.imperative: It occurs most often as a polite imperative asking for patience: Please bear with me.
usage.while_pattern: While introduces the action or situation requiring patience: Bear with us while we update the system.
usage.irregular_forms: Bear is irregular: bear, bore, borne. The past participle in this sense is borne, not born.
usage.spelling_warning: The correct expression is bear with me. Bare with me literally suggests becoming uncovered and is normally an unintended spelling error.
usage.tone: The phrase is polite but can sound formulaic in customer-service announcements.
usage.tolerance_relation: Bear alone can mean tolerate something unpleasant, while bear with asks someone to remain patient with a person or temporary situation.

ja: 人が説明・作業などを終えるまで辛抱して待つ
一時的な遅延・不便・混乱について我慢する
人が考えをまとめたり問題を処理したりする間、急かさずにいる
Bear with me. の形で、「少しお待ちください」「しばらくお付き合いください」と頼む
長い説明や複雑な話を最後まで聞くよう相手に求める
en: to remain patient with someone while that person finishes an explanation or task
to tolerate a temporary delay, inconvenience, or difficulty
to avoid rushing someone while they think or deal with a problem
in Bear with me, to ask someone to wait patiently for a short time
to ask a listener to continue paying attention through a long or complicated explanation

nuance.ja: bear with は、相手に不便・待ち時間・分かりにくい説明などを一時的に我慢してもらう表現である。Bear with me for a moment. は、話者が情報を確認する、考えをまとめる、操作を終えるなどの間、少し待ってほしいという丁寧な依頼になる。Please wait. よりも、「こちらの事情でご不便をかけるが、辛抱してほしい」という含みがある。If you’ll bear with me, ... は、説明が長い、または一見本題から外れて見えるものの、最後には意味が分かるので聞き続けてほしいときにも使われる。put up with は不快な人・状況を嫌々耐える否定的な響きが強いが、bear with は通常、一時的な状況に対して協力と忍耐を求める比較的丁寧な表現である。
nuance.en: Bear with asks another person to tolerate a temporary inconvenience, delay, or difficult explanation. Bear with me for a moment politely requests patience while the speaker checks information, organizes a thought, or completes a task. Compared with Please wait, it more clearly acknowledges that the speaker’s circumstances may inconvenience the listener and asks for cooperation. If you’ll bear with me can also introduce a long or apparently indirect explanation whose relevance will become clear later. Put up with often suggests reluctantly tolerating a persistently unpleasant person or situation, whereas bear with usually requests cooperative patience during a temporary difficulty.

ja: bear with：人が作業・説明などを終えるまで辛抱して待ち、一時的な不便を我慢する。
wait：ある時点・出来事まで行動せずにいる最も一般的な語。
be patient with：人や状況にいら立たず、辛抱強く接する。
put up with：不快な人・状況を嫌でも我慢する。
tolerate：好ましくない行為・状態などを許容し、耐える。
indulge：人の希望・癖などを寛大に受け入れる。文脈により甘やかす意味にもなる。
hold on：電話・会話などで、短時間待つよう求める口語表現。
give someone a moment：人が考える・確認するための短い時間を与える。
en: bear with means remaining patient with someone during a temporary delay, task, or explanation.
wait is the general verb for remaining inactive until a time or event.
be patient with means treating a person or situation calmly without becoming irritated.
put up with means reluctantly tolerating an unpleasant person or situation.
tolerate means accepting or enduring conduct or conditions that are undesirable.
indulge means allowing someone’s wish or habit generously and can also suggest excessive leniency.
hold on is an informal request to wait briefly, especially during a call or conversation.
give someone a moment means allowing a short time for the person to think, check, or finish something.

etymology.ja: bear は古英語 beran「運ぶ、担う、支える、耐える」に由来し、ドイツ語 tragen などと意味上比較できる古いゲルマン系の動詞である。物理的な重さを担う意味から、苦痛・困難・負担に耐える意味が発達した。bear with では、相手の遅れ・不完全さ・長い説明などを一時的な負担として受け止め、忍耐を保つという比喩的な意味になる。過去形は bore、過去分詞は borne であり、出生に用いる born とは区別される。
etymology.en: Bear comes from Old English beran, to carry, support, produce, or endure, and belongs to an old Germanic family of verbs involving carrying or bearing. The physical sense of carrying a weight developed into enduring pain, difficulty, or another burden. In bear with, a person’s delay, imperfection, or extended explanation is figuratively treated as a temporary burden that the listener patiently carries. The past tense is bore and the past participle in this sense is borne, which is distinct from born in expressions concerning birth.

note.ja: 人・作業・状況に対して、いら立たず辛抱強く接することを直接表す。
note.en: Directly means treating a person, task, or situation patiently and without irritation.

note.ja: 人・物・出来事が到着または完了するまで待つ。
note.en: To remain until a person, thing, or event arrives or is completed.

note.ja: 好ましくない行為・状態・不便などを許容し、耐える。
note.en: To accept and endure undesirable conduct, conditions, or inconvenience.

note.ja: 人の話・希望・行動などに、しばらく寛大に付き合う。
note.en: To accommodate a person’s wish, conduct, or explanation generously for a time.

note.ja: 電話中や作業中に、相手へ短時間待つよう求める口語表現。
note.en: An informal request for someone to wait briefly, especially during a call or task.

equivalents.de: mit jemandem Geduld haben / sich einen Moment gedulden
equivalents.es: tener paciencia con / esperar un momento

grammar.transitivity: transitive; the object may be a noun phrase, pronoun, wh-clause, or that-clause
patterns: bear it / this / that in mind
bear in mind what / how / why + clause
something should be borne in mind

usage.that_clause: Bear in mind that introduces a fact, limitation, or warning that should influence thought or action.
usage.noun_position: A short noun or pronoun commonly appears between bear and in mind: bear this in mind.
usage.long_object: A longer object or clause commonly follows the complete phrase: bear in mind the practical difficulties; bear in mind that costs may rise.
usage.gerund: Bearing in mind can introduce a relevant consideration: Bearing in mind the deadline, we should begin now.
usage.passive: The formal passive construction is should be borne in mind, using borne rather than born.
usage.memory_and_consideration: The phrase can mean remember, but usually suggests actively considering the information when deciding or acting.
usage.imperative: The imperative Bear in mind ... is common in advice, explanations, and warnings and may sound firmer than Please remember.
usage.register: Natural in both professional and everyday English; keep in mind is slightly more conversational.

ja: 重要な事実・条件・注意点を忘れずに覚えておく
判断・計画・行動をするとき、特定の事情を考慮に入れる
後で必要になる情報を意識にとどめておく
相手に重要な制約・例外・警告を念頭に置くよう求める
bearing in mind の形で、ある事情を考慮すれば
en: to remember an important fact, condition, or warning
to consider a particular circumstance when making a decision, plan, or judgment
to keep information consciously available because it will be relevant later
to ask someone to take account of an important limitation, exception, or caution
in bearing in mind, considering or taking account of a relevant fact

nuance.ja: bear in mind は、単に過去の情報を記憶しているだけでなく、その情報を現在または将来の判断・行動に反映させることを表す。Bear in mind that the deadline is Friday. は、金曜日という期限を覚えるだけでなく、作業計画をそれに合わせるよう促している。remember は情報を忘れないこと、consider はある事項について考えることを広く表す。take into account は複数の事情を評価・計算・判断へ具体的に組み入れる、より分析的な表現である。keep in mind は bear in mind とほぼ同義だが、やや会話的である。形式的な文章では It should be borne in mind that ... が使われるが、冗長に響くこともあるため、The court should consider that ... のように具体的な主語と動詞へ書き換えると明確になる場合がある。
nuance.en: Bear in mind means more than retaining information in memory; it usually requires allowing that information to influence a present or future decision or action. Bear in mind that the deadline is Friday asks the listener not only to remember the date but also to plan accordingly. Remember focuses on not forgetting information, while consider broadly means thinking about a matter. Take into account is more analytical and suggests incorporating a factor into an evaluation, calculation, or decision. Keep in mind is nearly synonymous with bear in mind but is somewhat more conversational. Formal writing sometimes uses It should be borne in mind that ..., although a direct construction such as The court should consider that ... may be clearer.

ja: bear in mind：重要な事実を覚えておき、判断・行動の際に考慮する。
keep in mind：bear in mind とほぼ同じで、やや会話的な「念頭に置く」。
remember：事実・経験・予定などを忘れずに記憶している、または思い出す。
consider：決定前に事情・選択肢・意見などをよく考える。
take into account：関連する要因を評価・計算・判断へ具体的に組み入れる。
take into consideration：事情・影響などを考慮する、やや形式的な表現。
be aware of：事実・問題・危険などの存在を知り、認識している。
not lose sight of：他の問題に気を取られても、重要な目的・事実を見失わない。
en: bear in mind means remembering an important fact and considering it when deciding or acting.
keep in mind is a slightly more conversational near-equivalent meaning to remember and consider.
remember means retaining or recalling a fact, experience, intention, or appointment.
consider means thinking carefully about a circumstance, option, or opinion before deciding.
take into account means incorporating a relevant factor into an evaluation, calculation, or decision.
take into consideration is a relatively formal expression for considering a circumstance or effect.
be aware of means knowing and recognizing the existence of a fact, problem, or danger.
not lose sight of means continuing to remember an important objective or fact despite distractions.

etymology.ja: bear は古英語 beran「運ぶ、担う、支える」に由来し、mind は古英語 gemynd「記憶、思考、心」にさかのぼる。bear something in mind は、ある事実や考えを心の中に「携えておく、保持する」という比喩に基づく。物理的な荷物を運ぶ bear が、責任・感情・考えなどを精神的に保持する意味へ広がった。過去形は bore、過去分詞は borne であり、受動形では It should be borne in mind. となる。
etymology.en: Bear comes from Old English beran, to carry, support, or sustain, while mind derives from Old English gemynd, memory, thought, or the faculty of thinking. Bear something in mind is based on the metaphor of carrying or retaining a fact or idea within one’s mind. The physical verb bear thus extended to the mental retention of a responsibility, feeling, or consideration. Its past tense is bore and its past participle is borne, producing the formal passive expression It should be borne in mind.

note.ja: 情報・条件などを忘れず、後の判断で考慮することを表す、やや会話的な表現。
note.en: A somewhat conversational expression meaning to remember information and consider it in a later decision.

note.ja: 事実・予定・経験などを記憶に保持する、または再び思い出す。
note.en: To retain or recall a fact, appointment, experience, or intended action.

note.ja: 関連する事情・数値・影響を評価や判断へ具体的に反映させる。
note.en: To incorporate a relevant circumstance, figure, or effect into an evaluation or decision.

note.ja: 決定・評価を行う前に、事実・選択肢・影響について注意深く考える。
note.en: To think carefully about a fact, option, or consequence before making a decision or evaluation.

note.ja: 警告・助言などに注意を払い、それに従って行動する形式的な語。
note.en: A formal verb meaning to pay attention to a warning or advice and act accordingly.

We should bear the additional maintenance costs in mind before purchasing the equipment. — その機器を購入する前に、追加の保守費用を考慮すべきである。

grammar.pos: complex preposition / adverbial phrase / predicative expression

forms.hyphenated_modifier: up-to-date / up-to-standard, only in established attributive compounds

grammar.transitivity: normally followed by a noun phrase, pronoun, number, or gerund; some uses are predicative
patterns: not be up to + noun / gerund

usage.maximum: Up to before a number expresses a maximum and normally includes that number: up to ten people means no more than ten.
usage.no_guaranteed_minimum: Up to states a ceiling but does not by itself guarantee any particular minimum.
usage.time: Up to can mean until a time or stage: up to the present; events leading up to the meeting.
usage.distance_level: It can indicate movement or extent as far as a place, person, level, or boundary.
usage.responsibility: Be up to someone means that the person has the responsibility or authority to decide.
usage.activity: Be up to something can mean be doing or planning something, often something secret, surprising, or possibly improper.
usage.ability: Not be up to something means lack sufficient strength, health, ability, or willingness for it.
usage.standard: Up to a standard means reaching the required level, commonly in be up to standard.
usage.gerund: After to in this expression, use a noun or gerund rather than an infinitive: Are you up to walking home?

ja: 数量・金額・程度などが最大で～まで
時間・段階・場所・高さなどが～まで
判断・選択・責任が人に委ねられて
人が何かをしている、または企んでいる
仕事・活動を行うだけの能力・体力・意欲がある
要求される基準・水準に達して
ある時点までに生じた事柄または進行した範囲
en: not exceeding a stated number, amount, or degree
as far as a particular time, stage, place, height, or limit
dependent on a person’s decision, choice, or responsibility
engaged in or planning an activity, sometimes secretly or suspiciously
having sufficient ability, strength, health, or willingness for a task
reaching a required standard or level
covering events or progress until a specified point

nuance.ja: up to は文脈によって意味が大きく変わる。up to ten people は「最大10人」で、通常10を含むが、10人参加することを保証せず、0人から10人までの可能性がある。It’s up to you. は「あなた次第です」「決定はあなたに任されています」を意味する。What are you up to? は中立的に「何をしているの」と尋ねる場合も、何かを企んでいると疑う場合もある。I’m not up to going out. は外出するだけの体力・気力がないという意味で、この to は不定詞標識ではなく前置詞なので going を用いる。The work is not up to standard. は仕事が必要水準に達していないことを表す。法律・広告などで上限を明確にする必要がある場合、up to だけでは最低値が示されないため、from X up to Y、up to and including Y などで範囲を明示することがある。
nuance.en: The meaning of up to changes substantially with context. Up to ten people means a maximum of ten and normally includes ten, but it does not promise that ten people will participate or establish any particular minimum. It’s up to you means that the choice or responsibility belongs to the listener. What are you up to? can neutrally ask what someone is doing or suspiciously ask what they are planning. I’m not up to going out means lacking sufficient energy, health, or willingness; to is a preposition here, so it is followed by the gerund going. The work is not up to standard means that it fails to reach the required level. In legal or promotional language, up to identifies a ceiling but not a floor, so from X up to Y or up to and including Y may be used when the full range requires clarification.

ja: up to：最大～まで、～次第で、～をしていて、または基準・能力に達して。
until：特定の時点まで状態・行為が続くことを表す。
as far as：場所・範囲・程度が～までであることを表す。
at most：数量・金額が多くてもその値を超えないことを明示する。
approximately：約、およそ。上限ではなく、数値の近似を表す。
depend on：結果・決定が人・条件・事情によって決まる。
capable of：行為を行う能力・性質があることを表す。
meet a standard：要求される基準・水準を満たす。
en: up to can mean a maximum, as far as a limit, someone’s responsibility, engaged in an activity, or capable of meeting a demand.
until indicates that an action or condition continues to a particular time.
as far as indicates the endpoint of movement, extent, range, or degree.
at most explicitly means that a number or amount cannot exceed the stated value.
approximately indicates an inexact value near a number rather than a maximum.
depend on means that an outcome or decision is determined by a person, condition, or circumstance.
capable of means having the ability or qualities required to perform an action.
meet a standard means satisfying a required level of quality or performance.

etymology.ja: up は古英語 up、upp「上へ」に由来し、to は古英語 tō「～へ、～まで」に由来する。物理的にある地点・高さへ向かい、その限界に到達するという組合せから、数量・時間・程度の「～まで」という意味が発達した。限界へ到達するという発想は be up to standard「基準まで達している」にも残る。責任・活動・能力を表す用法は、この空間的・限界的意味から比喩的に発達した。
etymology.en: Up derives from Old English up or upp, upward, while to comes from Old English tō, toward or as far as. Their combination originally indicated movement toward and arrival at a physical point or height. This spatial sense developed into the numerical, temporal, and scalar meaning as far as a particular limit. The image of reaching a level remains visible in be up to standard. The meanings involving responsibility, activity, and ability developed figuratively from these ideas of reaching, facing, or being equal to something.

note.ja: 数量・金額が指定された上限を超えないことを、up to より明示的に表す。
note.en: More explicitly states that a number or amount cannot exceed the specified maximum.

note.ja: 時間・出来事について、ある時点まで行為・状態が続くことを表す。
note.en: Indicates that an action or state continues to a particular time or event.

note.ja: 移動・範囲・程度が特定の場所・点・限界まで及ぶことを表す。
note.en: Indicates that movement, extent, or degree reaches a particular place, point, or limit.

note.ja: 決定・結果が特定の人や条件に左右されることを表す。
note.en: Means that a decision or outcome is determined by a particular person or condition.

note.ja: 特定の仕事・行為を行うための能力・体力・性質があることを表す。
note.en: Means having the ability, strength, or qualities required for a task or action.

grammar.transitivity: not applicable as an adjective phrase; tear is transitive or intransitive depending on sense
patterns: be torn between A and B
be torn between + noun and + noun
be torn between + gerund and + gerund
be torn between whether to do A or B, awkward
be torn as to whether + clause
feel torn between A and B

usage.between_pattern: The standard pattern for two competing alternatives is be torn between A and B.
usage.parallel_structure: The elements after between should normally have parallel forms: between staying and leaving.
usage.whether_pattern: For a full choice clause, use be torn over whether to do something or be unsure whether to do A or B.
usage.avoid_mixed_pattern: Be torn between whether ... is often awkward; use be torn between A and B or be torn over whether ... instead.
usage.emotion: The expression suggests that both alternatives exert a strong emotional or practical pull.
usage.predicative: Torn in this figurative sense is normally predicative: She was torn between the two offers.
usage.literal_sense: In a literal passive construction, be torn means be ripped or split: The document was torn.
usage.register: Natural in everyday, professional, and narrative English but less suitable than undecided or unable to determine in highly formal decisions.

ja: 二つ以上の選択肢の間で心が引き裂かれるように迷っている
相反する希望・義務・感情の双方に強く引かれている
どちらの選択にも重要な利点があり、決断できずにいる
忠誠・責任・価値観などの対立によって心が揺れている
文字どおりには、物が破られた・裂かれた状態にある
en: to be deeply undecided between two or more alternatives
to feel strongly pulled by conflicting desires, duties, or emotions
to have difficulty deciding because each option has important advantages
to experience emotional conflict between competing loyalties, responsibilities, or values
literally, to be in a state of having been ripped or split

nuance.ja: be torn は、単に情報不足で決められないというより、複数の選択肢がそれぞれ強い魅力・義務・感情を伴い、心が別々の方向へ引かれている状態を表す。I’m torn between staying and leaving. なら、残る理由と去る理由の双方が強く、容易に決断できないという意味になる。undecided は結論が出ていないことを中立的に表すが、torn は内面的な葛藤を強調する。ambivalent は同じ対象について肯定的感情と否定的感情を同時に抱くことが中心で、必ずしも二つの選択肢から選ぶ場面とは限らない。on the fence は立場や選択を決めずにいる口語表現で、be torn ほど強い感情的葛藤を示さない場合がある。なお、The paper was torn. では比喩ではなく「紙が破れていた」という文字どおりの受動表現になる。
nuance.en: Be torn suggests more than lacking enough information to decide. It presents the alternatives as exerting strong emotional, practical, or moral pulls in different directions. I’m torn between staying and leaving means that compelling reasons support both choices and make the decision difficult. Undecided neutrally states that no decision has been reached, whereas torn emphasizes internal conflict. Ambivalent primarily describes simultaneous positive and negative feelings about the same person, object, or proposal and does not necessarily involve a choice between two alternatives. On the fence is an informal expression for withholding a decision or position and may imply less emotional conflict than be torn. In The paper was torn, however, the construction is literal and simply means that the paper had been ripped.

ja: be torn：相反する選択肢・感情・義務の間で、心が引き裂かれるように迷う。
be undecided：まだ決定・結論を出していないことを中立的に表す。
be conflicted：相反する感情・価値観・義務を抱え、内面的に葛藤する。
be ambivalent：同じ対象について肯定的・否定的な感情を同時に持つ。
be divided：意見・忠誠・感情などが二方向に分かれている。
be on the fence：どちらの側・選択肢を支持するか決めずにいる。口語的。
face a dilemma：どちらを選んでも問題のある難しい選択に直面する。
waver：決心・意見・支持などが揺れ動く。
en: be torn means feeling strongly pulled between conflicting choices, emotions, duties, or loyalties.
be undecided neutrally means that a decision or conclusion has not yet been reached.
be conflicted means experiencing an internal struggle between incompatible feelings, values, or obligations.
be ambivalent means having both favorable and unfavorable feelings about the same subject.
be divided means having one’s opinions, loyalties, or emotions split in different directions.
be on the fence informally means not having chosen a side or alternative.
face a dilemma means confronting a difficult choice in which each available option has disadvantages.
waver means repeatedly changing or weakening in a decision, opinion, or commitment.

etymology.ja: torn は動詞 tear「引き裂く、破る」の過去分詞である。tear は古英語 teran「裂く、引き裂く」に由来し、ドイツ語 zehren などと歴史的に関係するゲルマン系の語である。物が二方向から引かれて裂けるという物理的なイメージから、人の心・忠誠・希望が相反する方向へ引かれる内面的葛藤を表す比喩が生じた。活用は tear–tore–torn であり、涙を意味する名詞 tear とは綴りが同じでも発音が異なる。
etymology.en: Torn is the past participle of tear, to rip or pull apart. Tear derives from Old English teran, to rend or tear, and belongs to a Germanic word family historically related to words including German zehren. The physical image of an object being pulled in opposing directions until it splits developed into a metaphor for a mind, loyalty, or desire pulled by incompatible alternatives. The verb forms are tear–tore–torn. The verb tear is pronounced differently from the identically spelled noun tear meaning a drop from the eye.

note.ja: 相反する感情・義務・価値観を同時に抱え、内面的な争いを感じている。
note.en: Experiencing an internal struggle between incompatible feelings, duties, or values.

note.ja: どの案・立場を選ぶか、まだ結論を出していない。
note.en: Not yet having reached a conclusion about which option or position to choose.

note.ja: 同じ対象に対して、好意と反感など相反する感情を同時に抱いている。
note.en: Having simultaneous favorable and unfavorable feelings toward the same subject.

note.ja: 意見・感情・忠誠などが複数の方向に分かれている。
note.en: Having opinions, emotions, or loyalties split between different directions.

note.ja: 二つの立場・選択肢のどちらを支持するか決めていない、口語的な表現。
note.en: An informal expression for not having decided which of two positions or alternatives to support.

ja: I’m torn between taking the new job and staying with my current team. — 新しい仕事を引き受けるか、現在のチームに残るかで迷っています。
She felt torn between her professional duties and her family responsibilities. — 彼女は職業上の義務と家庭での責任との間で葛藤していた。
We are still torn over whether to renovate the apartment or move elsewhere. — 私たちは、その部屋を改装するか別の場所へ引っ越すか、まだ迷っている。
He was torn because both proposals offered significant advantages. — どちらの提案にも大きな利点があったため、彼は決めかねていた。

The applicant was torn between narrowing the patent claim to obtain an early allowance and maintaining broader language for stronger protection. — 出願人は、早期の特許査定を得るため請求項を限定するか、より強い保護のため広い文言を維持するかで迷っていた。
en: I’m torn between taking the new job and staying with my current team.
She felt torn between her professional duties and her family responsibilities.
We are still torn over whether to renovate the apartment or move elsewhere.
He was torn because both proposals offered significant advantages.
The applicant was torn between narrowing the patent claim to obtain an early allowance and maintaining broader language for stronger protection.

forms.past_viewpoint: It was going to be all right.

patterns: I’m sure it’ll be all right.
Don’t worry; it’ll be all right.
It’ll all be right in the end, less common
Do you think it’ll be all right?
It’ll be all right if + clause
It’ll be all right once + clause
It’s going to be all right.

usage.contraction: It’ll is the contraction of it will and is especially common in speech and informal writing.
usage.future: Will presents the satisfactory outcome as a prediction or confident reassurance about the future.
usage.all_right: All right means satisfactory, safe, acceptable, or free from serious trouble in this expression.
usage.spelling: All right is the established two-word spelling; alright is widespread informally but may be avoided in edited formal writing.
usage.reassurance: The expression is commonly used to comfort someone who is worried, upset, ill, or facing difficulty.
usage.intonation: A calm falling intonation usually conveys confidence; uncertain or rising intonation can make the reassurance sound doubtful.
usage.it_reference: It may refer to a particular problem, the general situation, or an anticipated outcome.
usage.register: Natural in conversation; a formal context may require a more specific prediction or assessment.

ja: きっと大丈夫です
最終的には問題なく収まるでしょう
今は困難でも、状況はいずれ良くなるでしょう
心配するほど深刻な結果にはならないでしょう
相手を安心させるための「何とかなるよ」
en: the situation will probably have a satisfactory outcome
things will eventually be safe or free from serious trouble
the present difficulty will pass or become manageable
the feared result is unlikely to be as serious as expected
a reassurance meaning that there is no need to worry excessively

nuance.ja: It’ll be all right. は、不安や困難がある人に対して、状況は最終的に無事または満足できる形に落ち着くと伝える定型的な慰めの表現である。客観的な保証というより、話者の楽観・信頼・励ましを示す場合が多い。Don’t worry; it’ll be all right. は温かい励ましになり得る一方、深刻な問題に対して根拠なく使うと、相手の不安を軽視しているように響くこともある。Everything will be all right. は状況全体について、より包括的に安心させる。It’s all right. は現在の状態が問題ない、相手の行為を許す、または謝罪を受け入れる表現であり、未来の結果を予測する It’ll be all right. とは異なる。It’s going to be all right. は、状況が良い方向へ進んでいるという確信をやや強く感じさせることがある。
nuance.en: It’ll be all right is a conventional reassurance that a worrying or difficult situation will eventually reach a safe, manageable, or satisfactory outcome. It often expresses the speaker’s optimism, trust, or emotional support rather than an objective guarantee. Don’t worry; it’ll be all right can be warm and comforting, but if used without grounds in response to a serious problem, it may sound as though the speaker is dismissing the other person’s concerns. Everything will be all right offers broader reassurance about the entire situation. It’s all right refers to a present condition, grants permission, or accepts an apology, whereas It’ll be all right predicts a future outcome. It’s going to be all right may sometimes suggest slightly stronger confidence based on how the situation appears to be developing.

ja: It’ll be all right.：将来、状況はきっと無事・満足できる形に収まるという励まし。
It’s all right.：現在は問題ない、構わない、または謝罪を受け入れる。
Everything will be all right.：状況全体が最終的にうまくいくと、より包括的に安心させる。
It’ll be okay.：It’ll be all right. とほぼ同じ意味の、非常に一般的な口語表現。
Don’t worry.：相手に心配しないよう直接伝える。
You’ll be all right.：相手自身の健康・安全・状態が大丈夫になると励ます。
It should be all right.：おそらく大丈夫だが、一定の不確実性があるという予測。
Things will work out.：問題が時間とともに解決し、良い結果になると励ます。
en: It’ll be all right reassures someone that the future outcome will be safe, manageable, or satisfactory.
It’s all right says that the present situation is acceptable, grants permission, or accepts an apology.
Everything will be all right gives broader reassurance concerning the whole situation.
It’ll be okay is a very common conversational near-equivalent of It’ll be all right.
Don’t worry directly tells someone not to remain anxious.
You’ll be all right reassures the listener about their own health, safety, or condition.
It should be all right predicts an acceptable outcome while leaving some uncertainty.
Things will work out reassures someone that problems will eventually be resolved satisfactorily.

etymology.ja: It’ll は it will の短縮形で、will は古英語 willan「望む、意図する」に由来し、後に未来・予測を表す助動詞となった。right は古英語 riht「正しい、まっすぐな、公正な」に由来する。all right は文字どおりには「すべて正しい状態」を表し、そこから「問題がない、満足できる、無事である」という意味を発達させた。It will be all right. は、この状態が将来実現するという予測から、安心や励ましを与える定型表現となった。
etymology.en: It’ll is the contraction of it will. Will derives from Old English willan, to wish or intend, and later developed its auxiliary use for futurity and prediction. Right comes from Old English riht, correct, straight, or just. All right literally suggested that everything was in a correct condition and developed the senses satisfactory, free from trouble, and safe. It will be all right consequently became a conventional prediction used to provide comfort and reassurance.

note.ja: 将来の状況が問題なく収まると伝える、非常に一般的な口語表現。
note.en: A very common conversational reassurance that the future situation will be acceptable or manageable.

note.ja: 状況全体が最終的に良好な結果になると安心させる。
note.en: Reassures someone that the situation as a whole will ultimately have a satisfactory outcome.

note.ja: 現在の問題がやがて解決し、結果的にうまくいくと励ます。
note.en: Suggests that present problems will eventually be resolved successfully.

note.ja: 相手が困難な経験を耐えて乗り越えられると励ます。
note.en: Encourages someone by expressing confidence that they will survive and overcome a difficult experience.

note.ja: 心配する必要がないと、やや明示的・説明的に伝える。
note.en: States more explicitly that the circumstances do not require anxiety.

equivalents.de: Es wird alles gut. / Es wird schon gutgehen.

Everything will be all right.
I’m sure it’ll be all right.
Don’t worry; it’ll be all right.
It’ll be all right in the end.

It’ll probably be all right.

It’s going to be all right.

ja: Don’t worry about the journey; it’ll be all right once we get on the train. — 移動のことは心配しないでください。電車に乗れば大丈夫です。
The first few days may be difficult, but it’ll be all right. — 最初の数日間は大変かもしれませんが、きっと大丈夫です。
“I think I made a mistake.” “It’ll be all right—we can correct it together.” — 「間違えてしまったと思います」「大丈夫です。一緒に直せます」
